citations.anchor: rejects every verb but GET on /api/activity
citations.why: Drives POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE at the route and asserts 404 on each while GET is 200 — a writing route would answer something other than 404. The other half is now pinned by package-shape.spec.ts → “holds no statement that changes or removes a row”, which scans the package's own sources for `.update(activityEvents)` / `.delete(activityEvents)` and for raw UPDATE/DELETE against the table — a repair path or retention sweep would fail there while leaving every one of these 404s intact.

citations.anchor: workspace.created → { name, slug } against the workspace
citations.why: `toEqual({...base(), …})` pins the produced row's `id` to `EVENT_ID`, the source event's own id — a generated key would fail the equality.

citations.anchor: a re-delivered event does not double-record
citations.why: Un-stamps a delivered outbox row, drains twice, and asserts exactly one `user.invited` audit row remains — the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING clause is the only thing that makes that true.

citations.anchor: workspace.member_added → subject is the USER, meta { workspaceId, email }
citations.why: The `toEqual` includes `at: AT`, the event's `occurredAt`, so a row stamped with delivery time instead would fail.

citations.anchor: records user.signed_in on login and exposes it via the read API
citations.why: Asserts the item carries neither `createdAt` nor `created_at` — the 'never selected on a read' clause.

citations.anchor: returns null for an unmapped kind
citations.why: Pins the null outcome for a kind with no mapper; the spec runs with no database at all, so a mapper reaching for one would fail here.

citations.anchor: it.each(['workspace.member_added', 'workspace.member_removed'])
citations.why: The other outcome: an audited kind whose payload cannot name a subject throws `UnmappableAuditEventError` rather than returning null, so the two are provably not conflated.

citations.anchor: a non-string userId is refused too (not coerced)
citations.why: The membership mapper refuses rather than substituting a default — a coerced or empty `subjectId` would produce a row instead of the throw this asserts.

citations.anchor: parks the event instead of writing an empty-string subject
citations.why: End to end: a `workspace.member_added` outbox row with no `payload.userId` leaves no activity row at all and stays undispatched with attempts bumped.

citations.anchor: never repeats the actor inside meta — it owns two columns already
citations.why: Asserts `meta` has no `actor` property while `actorId`/`actorEmail` carry it — the lift-and-do-not-duplicate clause. The `via` merge clause is pinned by the same spec's “folds the actor’s `via` into meta without displacing it”, which asserts the merged object (the kind's own `name` beside `via`), with a control case proving an ordinary row carries no `via` key at all.

citations.anchor: never carries a secret or a hash into the audit row
citations.why: Feeds a `secret` and a `tokenHash` into the payload and asserts `meta`'s key set is exactly the four enumerated fields and the serialized row contains neither value.

citations.anchor: member.invited → user.invited { email }
citations.why: Pins the member.* → user.* rename for one kind; a passthrough would produce `member.invited`.

citations.anchor: auth.signed_in → user.signed_in, actor = the user
citations.why: Pins the auth.signed_in → user.signed_in rename.

citations.anchor: api_token.created → token.created on an api_token subject
citations.why: Pins the api_token.* → token.* rename; the `toEqual` fixes the produced `kind` exactly.

citations.anchor: media.asset.uploaded → media_asset subject, payload minus actor
citations.why: The 'the rest pass straight through' clause for one of the untouched families: an event of kind `media.asset.uploaded` must produce the identical audit kind.

citations.anchor: workspace.member_removed → subject is the USER, nullable email
citations.why: Asserts `subjectType: 'user'` and `subjectId` = the affected user for a workspace-membership event, with the workspace's id in `meta.workspaceId`.

citations.anchor: rejects an unauthenticated request with 401
citations.why: The session clause for GET /api/activity. Nothing pins /dead-letters, the /entries/:id route, or the refusal of an external API bearer token.

citations.anchor: forbids a contributor with 403
citations.why: The `activity:read` clause for GET /api/activity: a signed-in principal without the permission is refused.

citations.anchor: AND-composes the filter with the existing kind param
citations.why: A `kind` param plus an `actorEmail` `?filter=` tree must intersect: the asserted total of 1 is only reachable if the two compose with AND rather than one replacing the other.

citations.anchor: paginates with page/pageSize and echoes the envelope
citations.why: A request carrying no filters reports `total: 3`, the whole seeded set — the 'absence of filters gives the full set' clause.

citations.anchor: rejects an unknown field with 400 (whitelist)
citations.why: A `?filter=` naming `meta` is refused with 400 — pins the 'meta is not in the filterable surface' clause. The `createdAt` half and the count of eight are pinned by activity-filter.spec.ts (unit) → “offers eight columns and neither meta nor created_at”, which names all eight exhaustively — a swap keeps the count and changes the contract.

citations.anchor: filters by actor email (case-insensitive substring)
citations.why: Searches `ACTIVITY-ADMIN` against a lowercase address and gets all three rows — the case-insensitivity clause. The LIKE-metacharacter escaping clause is pinned by activity-filter.spec.ts (unit), which renders the built predicate with Drizzle's own PgDialect and asserts the bound parameter — `%` → `%\%%`, `_` and `\` likewise, and an ordinary address unchanged as the control.

citations.anchor: // `created_at` is internal and never reaches the wire.
citations.why: The two assertions under this line check the response item has neither `createdAt` nor `created_at`.

citations.anchor: shows no copilot-only tool, whatever the scope
citations.why: `tools/list` on a full-scope token is asserted not to contain `activity_recent` — the `surfaces: ['copilot']` clause. The `readOnly`/`effect: 'read'` markings are now pinned by activity-tool.provider.spec.ts, which reads the definition directly.

citations.anchor: is not callable by a contributor even if the model names it
citations.why: Executing `activity_recent` as a contributor (who lacks `activity:read`) fails — the 'requires the same permission as the route' clause, enforced at call time as well as at offer time.

citations.anchor: refuses both destructive routes with 503 while the counters read 0
citations.why: Boots a second app from the `omitContent` plugin list, which registers ActivityPlugin but neither CopilotPlugin nor McpPlugin — so no `ToolsModule` binds `ToolRegistry`. Dropping the `@Optional()` on `ActivityCopilotToolProvider` makes that boot fail and this test error out.

citations.anchor: a collapsed row contributes one table row, not two
citations.why: `getByRole('row')` (the accessibility tree) counts events + header while collapsed, and exactly one more after expanding — which only holds if the collapsed detail `<tr>` is aria-hidden/inert.

citations.anchor: comes back to the last page when a filter leaves fewer
citations.why: From `?page=3`, a filter narrowing 60 events to 1 drops `page` from the URL and shows the row — the 'does not stay beyond the last page' half.

citations.anchor: keeps a deep-linked page instead of resetting it on arrival
citations.why: With the response delayed, `?page=3` survives the first render — the 'does not discard a deep link before the first response' half.

citations.anchor: restores the filter from a deep link on load
citations.why: Navigating straight to `/activity?filter=…` reproduces the filtered table and the trigger's condition count, so the URL alone carries the state.

citations.anchor: deep-links the active search into the URL
citations.why: Typing in the actor-email search puts `actorEmail=` into the address bar rather than keeping it in component state only.

citations.anchor: workspace.archived → empty meta object (not null)
citations.why: The `toEqual({...base()})` pins `actorType: 'user'` for an actor that declares no `type`. The 'actorType is null iff actorId is' clause is now pinned by the same spec's “the actor columns move together” block: an event with no `attachActor` at all yields null on all three actor fields, and a token actor keeps `api_token` rather than being defaulted.

citations.anchor: lists every kind the server can produce
citations.why: Reads the admin's `ACTIVITY_KINDS` out of its source and asserts no server `AUDIT_KINDS` entry is missing from it.

citations.anchor: lists no kind the server cannot produce
citations.why: The other direction of the same set equality: no admin label without a server kind behind it.

citations.anchor: declares no kind no mapper can emit
citations.why: Drives every mapper in `AUDITED_EVENT_KINDS` and asserts each declared `AUDIT_KINDS` entry is actually produced — the 'reachable from some mapper' clause.

citations.anchor: compares against a dummy hash when no such account exists
citations.why: The unknown-address refusal still runs exactly one bcrypt comparison (`verifications` has one entry) and still ends in the same `InvalidCredentialsError` — recording the failure changed neither.

citations.anchor: refuses a pending invite the same way, opening no session
citations.why: A second refusal path: one comparison, the same error, no session, and exactly one `auth.sign_in_failed` event appended. The 'a failure to record is swallowed rather than turned into a 500' clause is unpinned.

citations.anchor: writes one row for two requests inside the same minute
citations.why: Two authenticated requests inside the throttle window leave exactly one `token.used` audit row and an unchanged `last_used_at` — the row follows the touch, not the traffic.

citations.anchor: writes a second row once the throttle window has passed
citations.why: The complement: back-dating `last_used_at` past `LAST_USED_TOUCH_INTERVAL_MS` produces a second row, so the throttle is what bounds the count rather than the row being dropped altogether.
